# Cascade (01, writer) — BAD-074

## Brief
Correct the render-diff recipe in
`/Users/ericlugo/Personal/Spud/docs/spikes/bad-036/admin-account-page.md`. That
recipe is section 8 step 5, and it is the primary proof for BAD-054 PR 2, which
does not start until this lands. As written it produces a false failure on every
run and a false pass on one of the three drifts section 10 names.

This is a documentation change with the investigation already done. Snowden (02,
reviewer) established every fact below while reviewing PR 1; your job is to write
them into the spike accurately, not to rediscover them. Where you can cheaply
confirm something, do.

**Three corrections, all in one pass.**

**1. The normalisation is incomplete (BAD-074, the ticket you are on).** Step 5's
perl strips `<script>` blocks and `relative()`'s outputs. Two build-fingerprinted
values survive it and differ between any two builds, so before and after always
diverge:

- the `/_next/static/` asset URLs in the head
- the Server Action ids in each control's hidden inputs, and the `ACTION-KEY`
  value alongside them

Snowden measured 532 diff lines from those alone, and proved they are build
artifacts rather than render differences with a control run: identical source
built at a second path produced exactly the same action-id differences and
nothing else, and all twenty ids in `.next/server/server-reference-manifest.json`
differ between two builds of the same source, including actions on pages the
split never touches. With the asset URLs, the action id and the `ACTION-KEY`
value normalised, pre-split and post-split are byte-identical across 76
documents.

**2. It misses `countdown()` (BAD-070, folded in here — close both).** The perl
normalises `relative()`'s shapes (`just now`, `Nm/Nh/Nd ago`) but not
`countdown()` in `@/lib/format.ts`, which emits `in Nh Nm` or `in Nm` and is
rendered by `Allowance` as ` · next {countdown(verdict.nextAt)}`. Two of the nine
seed accounts, cass and dev, are deliberately on cooldown, so those two pages
carry a live countdown that moves between captures. Dakota's extension is
`s#\bin \d+h \d+m\b#AGE#g; s#\bin \d+m\b#AGE#g`, and Snowden independently agreed
it is sufficient: both numeric forms are covered, the seeded cooldowns sit about
21 hours out so no boundary is crossed mid-run, and it applies to both phases.

**3. Section 10 makes a false claim.** It says the render diff catches a dropped
`key`. It cannot: React never writes a `key` into HTML, and the RSC payload that
does carry one lives inside the `<script>` tags the recipe strips. Snowden removed
the `key` prop from the usage rail's `Link`, rebuilt, and got zero difference
across all 76 documents — while the same build's wrong-side conditional
(`licenses.length > 1` changed to `> 0`) showed up immediately on eight user tabs.

The consequence has to be written down, not just the correction. In PR 1
`verify-moves.cjs` catches a dropped `key` only because the declaration moves
whole. In PR 2 it will not, because the components are rebuilt. So a dropped
`key` becomes a drift that **only reading the diff catches**, and section 10's
list of three silent drifts needs to say which check catches which: the render
diff catches a wrong-side conditional wrapper, reading the diff catches a dropped
`key` and a missing JSX comment, and nothing else catches either.

**Also update section 8's step 5 expected-result line and its "Why the
normalisation" bullets** so they match what the perl now does. Keep the recipe
runnable: it is copied and pasted by whoever runs PR 2, so the perl must be
correct as written, not approximately right. Syntax-check what you write
(`perl -e` with the substitutions against a sample string is enough) rather than
trusting the transcription.

Do not restructure the spike, renumber its sections, or revise anything outside
step 5, its "Why the normalisation" bullets, and section 10's silent-JSX-drift
bullet. Every other section is the approved plan for work in flight.

Note at the top of step 5 that the recipe was corrected against BAD-054 PR 1's
evidence, so the next reader knows the version they are looking at is the tested
one.

## Result
Rewrote section 8 step 5 and section 10's silent-JSX-drift bullet in /Users/ericlugo/Personal/Spud/docs/spikes/bad-036/admin-account-page.md; nothing else in the file changed (git status in Spud shows that one modified path, uncommitted). Step 5 now opens with a note that the recipe was corrected against BAD-054 PR 1's evidence, and its perl grew from two rules to six: the existing script strip and relative() rule, plus s#/_next/static/[^"\s>]+#/_next/static/ASSET#g, s#<input type="hidden" name="\$ACTION[^>]*>#<input type="hidden" name="ACTION"/>#g (one token per action input, which covers the id in $ACTION_ID_<id>, the id inside the bound $ACTION_<n>:<i> JSON, and $ACTION_KEY's value in a single rule while leaving every other hidden input alone), and Dakota's two countdown() rules verbatim. Expected-result line now says diff -r must print nothing across all 72 documents (9 accounts x 8 views) and points at section 10 for what it cannot see; the 'Why the normalisation' bullets now carry the evidence (532 diff lines, the twenty manifest ids, the second-path control build, the ~21h cooldowns). Section 10 now states which check catches which drift: the render diff catches a wrong-side conditional wrapper; only reading the diff catches a dropped key or a missing JSX comment, because React never writes a key into HTML and the RSC payload that carries one is inside the stripped script blocks; and it records that verify-moves catches a dropped key on PR 1 only because declarations move whole, so on PR 2 nothing but human reading catches it. Verified by extracting the block back out of the markdown: bash -n passes on the fenced block as written, and the perl program read from the file turns 7.2k chars of difference between two simulated builds (different chunk hashes, different action ids, different $ACTION_KEY, moved clock, different build id) into byte-identical output, while still catching a section that stops rendering and a control form that stops rendering; non-action hidden inputs survive. Sample built from the worktree's real .next/server/app/_not-found.html plus a form block in React's exact rendered hidden-input shape (confirmed from react-dom's pushAdditionalFormField and from the 20 x 42-hex ids in .next/server/server-reference-manifest.json). Not run against a live stack - that needs the local Supabase stack plus seed, which is step 5's own setup and belongs to whoever runs PR 2. Open question for Spud: Snowden's count was 76 documents, but the recipe's loop produces 72 (9 accounts x 8 views), so I wrote 72 and said 'every document in the run' where the count was cited; if Snowden fetched a wider set, the loop is what needs correcting, not the number.

That caught one wrong assumption (data-precedence carries no hash) and proved the six rules erase 7,234 characters of build noise while still failing a section that stops rendering. Its single ACTION rule covering the id, the bound JSON and ACTION_KEY at once is better than the three the brief implied.
